title: Rejected credentials stay latched in memory until restart
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:136-139` latches a credential rejection in memory with no rotation or automatic health reset in this slice.

Why not higher: documented; unsent creates fail and release their money.

Smallest fix: re-read credential health from the store on rotation, or reset the latch on an operator action. Verify a rotated credential is used without a restart.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Deletion and resolution validate external ids differently
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 19 (opus suggestion rated as a defect; round 2); PR #7 review-bot thread on `reconciliation.rs:616`; widened by the W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/deletion.rs:36` accepts `.` in an external id; `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:611-616` does not. A dotted provider id can pass delete and be refused by resolution evidence filtering; the audit found that a dotted id also marks the whole account pass incomplete.

Why not higher: the simulator never generates a dotted id.

Smallest fix: align both with the pinned opaque-id grammar. Verify an exact dotted correlator through confirmation and deletion, and rejection of malformed evidence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: An early release-probe failure writes no parent controls manifest
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run item 5 (fable R2 as P3; Manager P2); carried as W6 Run item 5. Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/controls.py:60` returns 1 when the direct helper probe fails, before writing the phase evidence file. The phase still exits nonzero, but the parent manifest and its pointers are missing.

Why not higher: the failure is not masked; only its evidence is incomplete.

Smallest fix: write a failing parent manifest with the child pointer before returning. Verify with a deliberate helper failure.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Malformed keys listing or any repeating per-row error ends the periodic pass and the engine
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 16 (fable P3 raised to P2, opus; round 1); widened by the W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `keys.as_array().context(...)` in `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:453` fails on a wrong-shape success, which ends the periodic component and the engine (`src/bin/engine.rs:64-75`). The audit found the same for any per-row error that repeats in the one-second pass.

Why not higher: only a wrong-shape provider success reaches it; it fails closed, with no invented absence and no money effect.

Smallest fix: handle malformed evidence and per-row errors locally (mark the pass incomplete) and keep the component running. Verify the pass continues after one malformed listing.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: W5 observer termination races the 20 ms sampler
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #6 review-bot thread (Minor); carried as W6 Run item 12. Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py:203` terminates the observer only while it is `idle`; a statement landing during a sample matches no row and the assertion fails before observer loss. Correct runs can fail.

Why not higher: fails closed; it cannot make a broken run green.

Smallest fix: poll, with a bound, until this observer is idle, then terminate only its PID. Verify by repeated runs of the case.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: New deficiency CHECK constraints have generated names
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 24 (fable; round 4). Evidence at b037383: the cause/clamped_sats and absorbed-time checks in `migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:95-97,132` have generated names, which later migrations may need to reference.

Fix: give them explicit names in a later schema migration, verified against `pg_constraint`.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Retained-history capacity: no receipt resource index, and housekeeping shares the single read checkout
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits; W4 audit item 9. Evidence at b037383: receipts are permanent and `idempotency_records` (`migrations/0001-core.sql:123-129`) has no `resource_id` index; `SETTLED_RETENTION` (`src/api/mod.rs:40`) and `operation_history` (`src/api/mod.rs:31-35`) aggregate receipts by `resource_id`. The API store has one read session with a 250 ms checkout bound (`src/entry.rs:46`) shared by customers and housekeeping. Measured at 20,000 settled operations and 1,000,000 receipts with three concurrent readers: housekeeping missed its checkout and the API exited 1. Each operations-list page also aggregates the whole history before its limit.

Why not higher: fails closed (exit, no wrong data); the measured scale is beyond the local profile.

Smallest fix: add a `resource_id` index (or a receipt-to-operation index) and bound the list aggregation by the page. Verify by rerunning the retention scale matrix at that size with three readers. Related: retired-history reads item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A transient accept() error stops the API
description:
Severity P2 (rating confirmed by the follow-up ledger review). Source: W5 audit item 4; carried as W6 Run item 8. Evidence at b037383: any `listener.accept()` error on the customer or operator listener (`src/api/mod.rs:1245`, `:1253`) ends `serve()` and the API exits 1 until an operator restarts it. Handlers go into an unbounded `JoinSet`, and no credential is needed to open connections, so descriptor exhaustion (`EMFILE`) from idle loopback connections is plausible.

Why not higher: connection exhaustion is an accepted outage class in the profile (`docs/scope.md`); no money or data loss, keyed replay recovers.

Smallest fix: log, back off and keep accepting on transient errors. Verify with an attributed transient accept failure.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A failed reread erases earlier reconciliation identifiers
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:603-604` replaces `provider_identifiers.reconciliation` with the latest search's set, which is empty after a failed or partial read, so ids found earlier (for example two candidates) disappear from the error details until a later complete search finds them again. The money flags (`in_progress`, `single_match`) are kept and nothing is attached.

Why not higher: no attachment or money effect; only operator-visible evidence is lost temporarily.

Smallest fix: keep the union of observed safe ids separately from the latest verdict. Verify with two candidates followed by a failed reread.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: D-12 still lists only fenced methods
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `attach_details` and `land_create` no longer check the generation fence themselves; they rely on the caller's guard (a fenced settlement, or the resolution's status guard in the operator receipt transaction). `docs/decisions.md` D-12 does not say so. Documentation only; every caller holds the guard.

Fix: amend D-12 to name the guard each caller holds.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Admin effective-tenant overrides require a UUID
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 18 (astra; round 2); PR #7 review-bot thread on `operator.rs:196`. Evidence at b037383: `src/api/operator.rs:195` parses the effective-tenant override as a UUID. API-6 and DOM-1 allow 1-128 characters from letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`, so a valid tenant id such as `agent-7` is refused before the scoped lookup.

Why not higher: ordinary enrolment generates UUIDs, so the supported path is unaffected.

Smallest fix: validate the pinned identifier grammar instead of UUID syntax. Verify non-UUID tenant scoping on live and retained targets, and privacy for malformed and unknown tenants.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A non-array rail reply stops the API
description:
Severity P2 (rating confirmed by the follow-up ledger review). Source: W5 audit item 2; carried as W6 Run item 7. Evidence at b037383: a 200 `/settlements` reply with valid JSON that is not an array fails `as_array().context("rail observation array")` (`src/api/funding.rs:133`), ends the funding watcher and the API exits 1 (`task_stopped`, `src/api/mod.rs:1236`; `src/bin/api.rs`). Transport errors, non-200, unparseable and oversized replies are retried (`funding.rs:140`).

Why not higher: only the trusted loopback rail adapter can produce it; no false credit; documented bounded failure handling (`docs/scope.md`), and a W4 lifecycle test uses this fault as its exit trigger.

Smallest fix: treat it as an unavailable observation and retry. The W4 test (`tests/postgres/w4_round2.py:163-178`) needs a new trigger. Verify a later valid observation is credited.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: rate_allowance's consume flag is always true
description:
Severity P3. Source: W5 audit item 10; carried as W6 Run item 11. Evidence at b037383: the only caller passes `true` (`src/api/mod.rs:199`), so the `consume` parameter (`:201`) and its branch (`:220`) are dead.

Fix: remove the parameter.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: An absent registered backend evicts a healthy commit observer
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run (fable, round 1); PR #6 review-bot thread on `accounting.rs:148`; carried as W6 Run item 1. Evidence at b037383: in `src/store/accounting.rs:127-155`, a missing activity row for one attempt's backend counts as lost observer visibility, closes a healthy observer and ends every other attempt's sample run.

Why not higher: accounting stays conservative (charges more, never less); no money effect.

Smallest fix: tell an absent attempt backend apart from hidden or failed observer evidence. Verify with two registered attempts where one backend exits, asserting the other keeps its exemption.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Identity-mismatch case is not isolated from state rejection
description:
Severity P3. Source: PR #6 review-bot nitpick (Trivial). Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/w5_accounting.py:94-99` injects the identity mismatch while the backend is `idle:ClientRead`, so those samples would be rejected on state even if the matcher ignored `backend_start`. Lines 113-116 still catch an identity-reporting or missing-flag regression.

Fix: inject the mismatch during SyncRep and assert no extra exemption.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Older PRV-41 conformance anchor points one line early
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 21 (fable; round 3). Evidence at b037383: the older PRV-41 row in `docs/conformance-map.md` links `02-provider-contract.md:1267` (a blank line) instead of 1268. Navigation only.

Fix: point the anchor at 1268.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Retired-history reads scan the permanent retired table
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 20 (opus; round 3). Evidence at b037383: `retired_operations` has only its id key (`migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:175-180`), while `operation_history` (`src/api/mod.rs:31-35`) filters it by `id::text` equality and tenant and unions it into detail and list reads. The table is permanent and grows.

Why not higher: cost at large retired volumes was not measured and is beyond the represented scale.

Smallest fix: measure representative aged histories, then add matching access paths or index-usable predicates. Verify detail and list bounds and privacy. Related: the retained-history capacity item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Periodic pacing ignores provider throttle hints across remaining account calls
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 17 (opus suggestion rated as a defect; round 1); widened by the W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: a throttled channel ends its page walk, but other account calls and the next one-second pass do not honour a longer retry hint (`src/engine/reconciliation.rs:321-356`, `src/bin/engine.rs:64-75`). The audit adds that the pass re-reads credential health in a transaction before every provider call.

Why not higher: absence handling fails closed; production pacing policy belongs to W8.

Smallest fix: in the pacing work, yield and coalesce account work using provider hints. Verify with an attributed throttle and the resulting call history.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Stale precommit accounting comment
description:
Severity P3. Source: W5 Run item 3 (opus R1); carried as W6 Run item 3. Evidence at b037383: the comment at `src/engine.rs:199` says elapsed precommit work is charged separately; the code charges the whole attempt minus the attributed standby wait. Comment accuracy only.

Fix: align the comment with the arithmetic.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Account-pass observations get the pass-end instant
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/engine/reconciliation.rs:358,375-376` stamps every enumerated resource with one instant taken after all pages, so an older present state can overwrite a newer state observation. Gone writes use their own read's instant.

Why not higher: not shown to change a money decision; later observations correct the state.

Smallest fix: stamp each page with the instant of its own read. Verify with a state change between pages.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: An operator observed resolution can bind an already attached machine
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/api/operator.rs:422` and `src/store/business.rs:480` merge into the existing machine on `(provider_account, external_id)` for the same tenant and post this operation's fee and unit debits.

Why not higher: the open-commitment unique index refuses it while that machine has an open commitment, and it needs an authenticated operator decision.

Smallest fix: refuse an external id already attached to another operation. Verify with an operator resolution naming an attached machine.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: F3: rail history beyond the 2 MiB response cap stops funding ingestion
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits (F3); W5 Run deferred work; carried in PR #6 and #7. Evidence at b037383: the rail simulator returns its whole retained history on `GET /settlements` (`src/api/funding.rs:120-131`), and the client refuses any reply over 2 MiB (`src/http.rs:106`), about 8,000 observations. Past that, every poll fails as `rail_observation_unavailable` (`src/api/funding.rs:140`), so new payments are never credited, also after a restart. `docs/scope.md` records the limit.

Why not higher: no false credit or money loss; replies fail closed and the cap is far beyond the local profile's volumes.

Smallest fix: bounded delivery (a cursor or pages) that keeps replay, idempotency and restart behaviour. Verify with a history over the cap that still credits a new observation. Related: the funding watcher reprocessing item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Legacy unresolved fixture's error text differs from the base literal
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 23 (opus; round 3). Evidence at b037383: `tests/postgres/w6_continuation.py:81` uses `engine restarted while operation was running`, while the base runtime used `interrupted by ordinary restart`. The migration never reads that text.

Fix: use the original literal, or say the text is not exact.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Backoff-budget probe has a 7 ms scheduling window
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #6 review-bot thread (Major); carried as W6 Run item 14. Evidence at b037383: the probe sleeps 1.993 s (`tests/postgres/w5.py:924`) and requires `1990 <= spent_ms < 2000` (`:932`); a scheduling delay over about 7 ms takes the fatal path before any retry, and the required selector fails.

Why not higher: false reds only; no broken run passes.

Smallest fix: a controlled retry clock or a test hook at the budget boundary, without changing the runtime budget. Verify by injecting scheduling delay.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Activation without a healthy provider account is never assigned later
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 audit item 5; carried as W6 Run item 9. Evidence at b037383: activation inserts the only tenant-to-account assignment and just traces `activation_without_healthy_assignment` when no healthy account can be assigned (`src/api/funding.rs:81-88`), so the tenant keeps no provider account after accounts recover.

Why not higher: only fixtures change account status; whether the specification requires a later assignment is not yet assessed.

Smallest fix: assess the pinned specification first; then add the later assignment or document the limit with an account-recovery scenario.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A fence held by another episode closes the current one as funded
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/store/deletion.rs:82-94` closes the current cleanup episode as funded when the machine's fence belongs to another episode.

Why not higher: not shown reachable: each machine has at most one open delete episode and every close clears its fence.

Smallest fix: refuse or stall when the fence names another episode. Verify with a fixture holding a foreign fence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Commit observer reconnect and error churn without backoff
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run (opus P2, fable P3); PR #6 review-bot thread on `accounting.rs:182`; carried as W6 Run item 2. Evidence at b037383: a failed checked reconnect retries on every 20 ms tick, even with nothing registered (`src/store/accounting.rs:159-197`), producing dozens of connect and log cycles in about 2.2 s in the mismatch runs.

Why not higher: availability and log noise; no wrong charge shown.

Smallest fix: pace reconnect failures and coalesce diagnostics within the existing bounds. Verify a bounded attempt and log count during a persistent failure, and recovery afterwards.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Upgraded machines' pre-upgrade time is absorbed as a rate outage
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:116-121` seeds the rate history at migration time, so exit accounting finds no rate in force before the upgrade and records that span as an operator `rate_outage` deficiency instead of a customer debit.

Why not higher: only a schema-2 database with billable machines reaches it, and none is deployed.

Smallest fix: seed the rate history from each machine's frozen terms at its meter seed. Verify by upgrading a schema-2 fixture with a billable machine and checking its exit accounting.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Balance totals and commitments are read in two snapshots
description:
Severity P1 (older than this change; re-rated from a deferred known limit). Source: PR #5 known limits (WIR-16); carried in PR #6 and PR #7. Evidence at master b037383: `GET /v1/balance?commitments=true` reads its totals in one statement (`src/api/mod.rs:944`) and its commitments page in another (`src/api/mod.rs:949-951`, `page` at :971). A create or settlement committing between the two breaks WIR-16's `committed_sats == sum(reserved_sats)` (spec 13-wire-contract.md:652-655): a caller sees a body whose totals contradict its own commitments.

Why P1: wrong behaviour in a supported read (a wire invariant made false). Not P0: no money moves, the read is advisory.

Smallest fix: read totals and the page in one snapshot (one REPEATABLE READ transaction, or one statement). Verify with a test that commits a create between the two reads and asserts the equality.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Funding watcher reprocesses the whole rail history every 100 ms
description:
Severity P2 (re-rated from P3 by the follow-up ledger review for linear database and log load; the W6 Run report still lists it as P3). Source: W5 audit item 8; carried as W6 Run item 10. Evidence at b037383: every 100 ms tick (`src/api/funding.rs:142`) re-runs each retained final observation, credited or not: a binding read, a write transaction with the tenant serialization lock and COMMIT, and a trace line (`src/api/funding.rs:133-135`), on the API's single read and write sessions. 1,000 retained observations give about 10,000 transactions and trace lines a second.

Why not higher: no customer refusal was measured; the watcher releases its session between observations.

Smallest fix: skip observations already credited, or use a delivery cursor, preserving replay semantics. Verify bounded transactions per tick with a large credited history. Related: the F3 rail-history item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Raw W5 external-effects label omits w5
description:
Severity P2. Source: W5 Run item 4 (Implementer); PR #6 review-bot outside-diff comment; carried as W6 Run item 4. Evidence at b037383: the manifest predicate at `tests/postgres/harness.py:451` labels phase `w5` "not applicable: no external effects" although W5 records nested simulator effects. The evidence manifest therefore states something false about W5.

Why not higher: nested effects stay recorded and the sanitized summaries are correct.

Smallest fix: add `w5` to the simulator-evidence branch of the label. Verify by asserting the W5 manifest's classification.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Stale publication sentence in the W5 report
description:
Severity P3. Source: W5 publication audit; carried as W6 Run item 6. Evidence at b037383: `evidence/w5/report.md:20` says "Nothing was pushed, merged or published.", true when recorded and false since PR #6 merged. Wording only.

Fix: date the sentence or add a publication note, without changing the recorded evidence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: A legacy machine without native terms stops the engine at its cleanup
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/store/deletion.rs:91` treats missing native terms as no rate, so the cleanup reaches the stopped no-rate path and exits the engine.

Why not higher: same no-fence, no-call stop as the no-rate item; only legacy rows lack terms and none is deployed.

Smallest fix: give legacy machines their terms at migration or classify them separately. Verify with a legacy machine queued for cleanup. Related: the no-rate engine-exit item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Provider evidence can be frozen before the simulator's last record
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #6 review-bot thread (Minor); carried as W6 Run item 13. Evidence at b037383: the simulator records `read_response_returned` after the reply is delivered (`tests/postgres/simulator.py:281`), so the snapshot in `tests/postgres/w5.py:354-365` can miss it and the later exact equality fails.

Why not higher: fails closed on a missing final event.

Smallest fix: wait for the attributed completion record before freezing evidence, here and in the other full-trace comparisons. Verify by delaying the record in the simulator.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Meter quarantine does not stop the cleanup funding decision
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/store/deletion.rs:55-58` derives runway from the meter of a quarantined machine before fencing, while LDG-72 quarantines exhaustion decisions for that subject.

Why not higher: quarantine is set only by the migration audit.

Smallest fix: check quarantine before the funding decision and hold the cleanup. Verify with a quarantined machine queued for cleanup.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Retirement table header comment omits the new kind and machine metadata
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 25 (opus; round 6). Evidence at b037383: the header comment in `migrations/0003-reconciliation.sql:173-180` describes only identity, ownership and horizon, while `kind` and `machine_id` now support retained validation; the inline comment explains them.

Fix: make the header and inline comment agree.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Request headers are read one byte per syscall
description:
Severity P3. Source: W5 audit item 10; carried as W6 Run item 11. Evidence at b037383: `src/http.rs:25-28` reads headers one byte per `read` call, up to 16 KiB per request. No behaviour change required.

Fix: buffer the reads, preserving the header limits.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Schema-2 descriptor snapshots fail the new descriptor validation
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 publication audit. Evidence at b037383: `src/pricing.rs:278` now requires `delete_shape`, `surviving_attachments` and `negative_seconds`; queued creates admitted under schema 2 fail at dispatch after the upgrade, and old provider descriptors refuse startup.

Why not higher: fails closed, and no schema-2 database is deployed.

Smallest fix: migrate stored snapshots and descriptors to the new fields, or default them on read. Verify a schema-2 queued create dispatches after the upgrade.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: An excluded no-rate cleanup decision exits the whole engine
description:
Severity P2. Source: W6 Run item 15 (fable, opus; round 1). Evidence at b037383: when a cleanup reaches the no-rate decision (`src/engine/deletion.rs:63-66`), it traces `delete_no_rate_stopped` and returns `fatal`, so the error propagates out of the engine and stops all other work. Test: `tests/postgres/w6.py:370-375`.

Why not higher: the stopped path writes no fence and makes no provider call, so no money moves; only fixtures write rates, and OPS-41 steps 4-5 are left out by decision (D-46).

Smallest fix: when the no-rate lifecycle is in scope, isolate the stopped path so unrelated work continues. Verify unrelated work continues after a no-rate stop. Related: the legacy-machine-without-terms item.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: Dispatch deadlines come from the startup descriptor, not the frozen terms
description:
Severity P2. Source: PR #5 known limits; W5 Run deferred work. Evidence at b037383: `Dispatcher::load` reads every provider descriptor once at engine start (`src/engine/dispatch.rs:13-26`) and dispatch takes its deadlines from that catalog (`src/engine/dispatch.rs:218`), not from the terms frozen at admission. A descriptor change plus a restart between admission and dispatch can make a provider call wait longer than its reserve priced.

Why not higher: descriptors change only by operator configuration; no supported path changes them mid-flight.

Smallest fix: take dispatch deadlines from the admission's frozen terms. Verify by changing the descriptor between admission and dispatch and asserting the frozen deadline is used.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).

title: DOM-21 conformance row still says the receiptless gap remains
description:
Severity P3. Source: W6 Run item 22 (opus; round 3). Evidence at b037383: `docs/conformance-map.md:290` says "receiptless gap remains", which W6's receiptless retirement (retired identities that read as gone) has made stale. Status prose only.

Fix: update the row against the retained-identity evidence.

Listed in the known limits of PR #7 (https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond-rust/pull/7).
